questions.why: The ordered run is on the card for all fourteen endings; the only stretch it does not sequence is a call that changes nothing, and each of those says so where it sits — on this door both read "one return".

Every check that can refuse now sits in its place with a passed-or-stopped mark, and the app band stops being drawn backwards; the two helpers that run on every request and can refuse nothing still leave no row, and that roster is part of "inside-the-calls".

The through-route is read off the checks — "first run" passes all ten — and every other route names the one check that stopped it; how often each route is really taken cannot be read from code at all and stays out of the tool.

Three of the four things that decide a path — the door's own guard, the fork one call down, the setting chosen before the request arrived — are already labels on the run; the failures raised two calls deeper are recorded with their condition and still not loaded.

The run gives every table touch a numbered spine to sit on, but what an individual touch depends on is still a yes-or-no flag — 38 of the 92 database steps on the first-run route are marked conditional with no condition written.
